sources.authors: G. Koch, N. Nadirashvili, G. Seregin, V. Sverak
sources.title: Liouville theorems for the Navier-Stokes equations and applications
sources.claim_used: For a mild solution launched from bounded data u_0, t^(k/2+l) nabla^k partial_t^l u is bounded by C(k,l)||u_0||_infinity on a time interval of length epsilon(k,l)||u_0||_infinity^(-2).

sources.authors: G. Koch, N. Nadirashvili, G. Seregin, V. Sverak
sources.title: Liouville theorems for the Navier-Stokes equations and applications
sources.claim_used: An ancient mild solution is mild on R^3 x (T_j,0) from its value at T_j for a sequence T_j tending to minus infinity; semigroup splitting at an interior smooth time permits the bounded-mild estimate to restart there.

sources.title: On local Type I singularities of the Navier-Stokes equations and Liouville theorems
sources.claim_used: For every parabolic ball Q(z,R), E(Q)=R^(-1) integral_Q |nabla u|^2 and I is the supremum of the nonnegative sum A+C+D+E over parabolic subballs, so finite I gives integral_Q |nabla u|^2 <= I R.

direct_calculation.temporal_persistence: If K=||partial_t omega||_infinity and |omega(x,t)|>lambda, then |omega(x,s)|>lambda/2 for t-delta<=s<=t when delta<=lambda/(2K).
direct_calculation.measure_step: Integrate the lower bound lambda^2/4 over the persistent superlevel cylinder and compare with the finite-I upper bound 2 I R.

source_nonclaims: The sources do not state that finite I implies a radius-free global weak-L^(3/2) vorticity bound.
The sources do not supply a summable annular vorticity tail, no-incoming theorem, one-profile morphology, or vorticity-direction certificate for this producer.
The sources do not prove Navier-Stokes regularity or close the Clay problem.
